comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FINDING from the S1/S2 code now on the branch — record before this plan is reviewed, because the plan as written would regress an existing test.

S1 (7468, closed) made runner.run() resolution THREE-WAY: (a) a provider in ProviderSession._builders is EAGERLY built via infer_model(provider_factory=...); (b) a provider pydantic-ai recognizes but rebar does not build is left as a LAZY model STRING; (c) neither => typed LLMConfigError. Today _builders holds ONLY 'anthropic', so 'openai' takes path (b).

That matters because the openai SDK is NOT installed (verified: importlib.util.find_spec('openai') is None; rebar's [agents] extra deliberately omits it, and pydantic_ai.providers.openai raises ImportError at import). S1's implementer already hit this once: calling infer_model unconditionally broke tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py's parameterized 'openai:gpt-4o' case (line 358), which stubs _pai_structured precisely so no real provider is ever constructed. It was fixed by gating eager construction on supports()/is_resolvable().

So if S4 simply registers an 'openai' builder in _builders, supports('openai') becomes True and EVERY 'openai:...' model string — including ones with no base_url, and including that existing test — would take the eager path and hit the missing-SDK ImportError. The plan says the builder is 'gated behind the opt-in pydantic-ai-slim[openai] extra with a clear missing-extra error', which is right for the intended use but would convert a currently-passing test into a hard failure.

The plan needs to state which of these it does, because they are materially different: (1) register 'openai' only when cfg.base_url is set (base_url is the opt-in signal, and the plan already insists base_url is provider CONFIGURATION not SELECTION, so this does not make base_url a selector); (2) register unconditionally but have the builder fall back to pydantic-ai's own infer_provider when no base_url is configured, preserving path (b) exactly; or (3) register unconditionally and add the [openai] extra to the dev/test env, which changes rebar's dependency posture and should be an explicit decision, not a side effect.

Recommend (1) or (2). Also note S4 targets providers.py, which is at 225 LOC against the 300-LOC cap that is an ATTESTED acceptance criterion of closed story S1 — so the builder must be small or live elsewhere. And S4's line citation ':653' for _pai_check_config is stale after S1/S2; it is now at runner.py:718.

comments.body: AC -> TEST MAP (the discipline added after f184 closed late with half a criterion untested). tests/unit/test_openai_compatible_provider.py, 11 tests: AC1 documented recipe end-to-end => test_documented_local_server_recipe_returns_a_structured_verdict; AC2 base_url must not hijack selection => test_base_url_does_not_hijack_provider_selection; AC3a refusal gone => test_check_config_accepts_a_valid_base_url; AC3b api_key without base_url => test_api_key_without_base_url_is_a_config_error; AC3c non-absolute base_url => test_non_absolute_base_url_is_a_config_error; AC3d missing extra names install cmd => test_missing_openai_extra_raises_naming_the_install_command; AC4 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway pin => test_non_loopback_anthropic_base_url_is_respected_as_a_gateway; AC5 override applied => test_custom_endpoint_withdraws_native_structured_output; AC6 override surgical => test_profile_override_is_surgical; AC7 bare openai builds no provider => test_bare_openai_string_without_base_url_builds_no_provider; plus contrast case test_native_output_still_selected_for_a_hosted_openai_model (the withdrawal must not leak to the hosted API). AC8 (providers.py<300 LOC, no openai branch in runner.py), AC9 (agents extra unchanged) and AC10 (lint/typecheck/full make test) are verified by grep/wc/CI rather than unit tests. MECHANISM CORRECTION recorded in the plan: the profile override rides the PROVIDER (a rebar OpenAIProvider subclass overriding the model_profile staticmethod), NOT OpenAIChatModel(profile=...) — because rebars S1 seam returns a Provider and infer_model builds the model itself, so a model-level argument is unreachable from the seam. pydantic-ai resolves profile=profile or provider.model_profile; verified end-to-end that the subclass yields model.profile.supports_json_schema_output False while supports_tools stays True, surviving the OpenAIModelProfile.update() applied afterwards. RED evidence: 6 failed for the right reasons (2x the actual loud refusal LLMConfigError does-not-yet-support, 2x assert True is False for the missing override, 1x wrong error text, 1x DID NOT RAISE), 5 passing are regression guards that must STAY passing.

# S4 — Best-effort OpenAI-compatible endpoint: honor REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL, retire the loud refusal

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:718` (`_pai_check_config`) raises on any `base_url`/`api_key`, while
`docs/llm-framework.md:126-133,226` documents both as working and shows an LMStudio/Ollama recipe, and
`src/rebar/llm/config.py:502-503,611-612` already parses them. The documentation is false today. The refusal was
a deliberate placeholder: commit `75e598a41` describes it as "a loud guard that REFUSES base_url/api_key rather
than silently dropping them (a capability gap vs langgraph, surfaced not hidden)". This story fills the
placeholder it was created for.

## Approach

Register an `openai` builder in the provider factory [rebar:7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1] that constructs
`OpenAIChatModel` with `OpenAIProvider(base_url=cfg.base_url, api_key=…)`, gated behind the opt-in
`pydantic-ai-slim[openai]` extra with a clear missing-extra error. Crucially, `base_url` is provider
**configuration**, not provider **selection**: the provider still comes from the model string /
`REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER`, exactly as `docs/llm-framework.md:132` already documents
(`REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL=…`). ### Capability handling for an opaque endpoint — the builder OVERRIDES the profile

An earlier draft of this plan claimed capability handling "comes free from S2 — an opaque endpoint resolves to
the conservative record". **That was false**, and the correction matters because it decides whether local
servers work at all. Verified against the code S2 landed:

- `capabilities_for()` reads `.profile` off a model OBJECT first, and this story's builder produces a real
  `OpenAIChatModel`, whose profile is the genuine OpenAI one.
- `openai_model_profile("local-model").supports_json_schema_output` is **`True`** (verified), so even the
  string path resolves through `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS["openai"]` to a native-capable record.

Either way the endpoint would get `NativeOutput` — strict `json_schema` constrained decoding — which an
arbitrary OpenAI-*compatible* server (Ollama, LMStudio, vLLM, a LiteLLM proxy) has no obligation to implement
faithfully. The failure mode is a silent wrong answer or an opaque parse error, exactly what this story must
not ship. The conservative fallback never fires here, because a key DOES match.

**Fix: the override rides the PROVIDER, not a model argument.** This distinction is forced by S1's seam and is
not a style choice. `OpenAIChatModel.__init__` does accept `profile: ModelProfileSpec | None`, but rebar's
factory hands back a **`Provider`** and pydantic-ai's `infer_model` constructs the model itself — so a
model-level argument is unreachable from the seam. pydantic-ai resolves
`super().__init__(profile=profile or provider.model_profile)` (verified in the pinned source), which means a
Provider that supplies its own `model_profile` flows straight through `infer_model` to `model.profile`.

So the builder returns a small rebar subclass of `OpenAIProvider` overriding the `model_profile` staticmethod to
return `dataclasses.replace(openai_model_profile(model_name), supports_json_schema_output=False)`. Every other
capability is inherited from upstream and only the strict-output claim is withdrawn.

Verified end-to-end against the pinned pydantic-ai: building `OpenAIChatModel("local-model", provider=<that
subclass>)` yields `model.profile.supports_json_schema_output is False` while
`model.profile.supports_tools` stays `True` — i.e. the withdrawal survives the `OpenAIModelProfile(...).update()`
that `OpenAIChatModel.__init__` applies afterwards, and it is surgical.

The justification is not squeamishness: the OpenAI profile describes OpenAI's **hosted API**. A custom
`base_url` is by definition a *different server* that merely speaks the same wire protocol, so upstream's
strict-output flag is not evidence about it. Withdrawing that one flag makes the plan's original claim true **by
construction** rather than by assumption, and it needs no change to S2's `capabilities_for()` and no per-call
boolean — preserving both S2's "the profile is the single source of truth" invariant and this story's rejection
of PR #121's `force_prompted`.

### WHEN the `openai` builder is registered — resolved, not left to the implementer

S1 (`7468`, closed) made `run()` resolution three-way: a provider in `ProviderSession._builders` is **eagerly**
built via `infer_model(provider_factory=...)`; a provider pydantic-ai recognizes but rebar does not build is
left as a **lazy model STRING**; a name neither resolves raises `LLMConfigError`. Today `_builders` holds only
`anthropic`, so `openai` takes the lazy path.

The `openai` SDK is **not a runtime dependency**: the `agents` extra deliberately omits it (see the
dev/test-dependency decision below, which adds it to `dev` ONLY), and `pydantic_ai.providers.openai` raises
`ImportError` without it. S1's implementation already hit the eager-construction hazard this creates: calling
`infer_model` unconditionally broke the parameterized `openai:gpt-4o` case in
`tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, which stubs `_pai_structured` precisely so no real provider is ever
constructed.

**The principled reason for conditional registration does not rest on SDK absence at all**, so it survives the
SDK being present in the dev env: with no `base_url` configured, rebar has *nothing to contribute* to provider
construction — no endpoint to inject, no key to place, no profile to override. Interposing a rebar builder that
merely reconstructs what pydantic-ai would have built anyway adds a maintenance surface and a divergence risk
for zero benefit. rebar builds a provider only when it has configuration to apply. That is the same rule S1
established (it builds Anthropic because it injects a retrying transport) and it is why `base_url` is the
correct trigger.

**Decision: the `openai` builder is registered ONLY when `cfg.base_url` is set.** A bare `openai:gpt-4o` with
no `base_url` keeps taking S1's lazy-string path, byte-for-byte as today, so no currently-passing test changes
behavior and no optional SDK becomes mandatory.

This does **not** make `base_url` a provider selector, which the plan rightly forbids. The provider is still
chosen by the model string / `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER`; `base_url` only decides whether rebar constructs that
provider *itself* (to inject the endpoint) or defers to pydantic-ai. The documented recipe at
`docs/llm-framework.md:131-133` sets `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai` **explicitly alongside**
`REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL`, so this matches rebar's own published contract exactly.

Rejected alternatives: registering unconditionally (breaks the existing test above and makes the `openai`
extra a hard requirement), and adding `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]` to the dev/test env (a change to rebar's
dependency posture that deserves its own decision, not a side effect of this story).

### The `openai` SDK is a DEV/TEST dependency here, not a runtime one

`pyproject.toml` states the project's position explicitly — "Additional model providers are opt-in (keep the
default extra lean)", with `[anthropic]` the primary provider SDK and OpenAI/Google opt-in. This story does NOT
change that: the `agents` extra stays lean and users of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint still opt in with
`pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[openai]'`, which the builder's missing-extra error names.

But the tests cannot be meaningful without it — `OpenAIChatModel` is unimportable without the SDK, so neither
the builder nor the end-to-end recipe can be exercised, and the acceptance criteria would only ever be provable
on a developer's machine while CI silently skipped them.

**Decision: add `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]` to the `dev` extra only.** There is direct precedent in this file:
`dev` already installs `mcp`, which is likewise an OPTIONAL runtime extra (`[mcp]`), precisely so its tests can
run in CI. Runtime posture is unchanged — `[agents]` does not grow, and nothing becomes mandatory for a user
who never points at a custom endpoint. What changes is only that CI can prove this story works.

This is deliberately narrower than the alternative the earlier draft rejected: that alternative was adding the
extra so the builder could be registered UNCONDITIONALLY (making the SDK effectively required). Registration
stays gated on `cfg.base_url`; this is purely about the test environment.

**Size budget:** `providers.py` is 225 LOC against the **300-LOC cap that is an attested acceptance criterion
of closed story S1**. The builder must fit, or move to a leaf of its own — it must not silently breach a signed
criterion.

`_pai_check_config` stops refusing and instead validates: an absolute-URL check on `base_url`, and an
`api_key`-without-`base_url` error (ambiguous, since the direct OpenAI path reads `OPENAI_API_KEY`). For a
no-auth local server an explicit placeholder key is sent so construction succeeds; a hosted endpoint answers
with its own 401.

This story also **documents the accidental capability** found during design: a non-loopback `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`
already routes rebar through an Anthropic-wire gateway, because `anthropic_model.py:60`
(`_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`) only overrides loopback hosts and the SDK reads the env var. It works today by
accident; this story makes it deliberate and tested.

**Alternative rejected:** branching on `cfg.base_url` before provider inference (PR #121's shape). That makes
`base_url` silently override an explicit `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER`, contradicting rebar's own documented
recipe, and adds a fourth implicit provider selector alongside the model string, the provider env var, and
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` — the `openai` builder.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — `_pai_check_config` (**`:718`**; the plan originally cited `:653`, stale
  after S1/S2 moved code) becomes validation.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — composition semantics for `base_url` + `model_provider`.
- `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` — replace `test_unsupported_config_is_a_loud_error`.
- `tests/unit/test_openai_compatible_provider.py` (new).
- `pyproject.toml` — `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]` added to the **`dev`** extra ONLY (the `agents` runtime extra
  stays lean); see the dev/test-dependency decision above.

## Testing

Contract tier: the defect class is a consumer (the runner) reading configuration the wrong way, so the test must
run through real config resolution rather than calling the builder directly.

- happy path: `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai` + `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1` yields an
  `OpenAIChatModel` whose provider carries that exact base URL and the configured api_key.
- contrast case (the PR #121 regression this exists to prevent): `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=anthropic` +
  `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL=…` still resolves the **anthropic** provider — base_url must not hijack selection.
- failure paths: `api_key` without `base_url` raises `LLMConfigError`; a non-absolute `base_url` raises naming
  the variable; a missing `openai` extra raises naming the install command.
- edge: no api_key + a local base_url constructs successfully with the placeholder key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the exact recipe printed at `docs/llm-framework.md:131-133` runs end-to-end against a local
      OpenAI-compatible server (or a stub server in-test) and returns a valid structured verdict
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=anthropic` + `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` resolves the anthropic provider
- [ ] `_pai_check_config` no longer raises for a valid `base_url`, and its three validation errors each have a test
- [ ] a test pins the `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` non-loopback gateway behavior so it can no longer change by accident
- [ ] a test asserts a model built by this builder yields `native_structured_output=False` from
      `capabilities_for()` and therefore `PromptedOutput` — i.e. the profile override is actually applied, NOT
      inherited as `True` from upstream's hosted-API profile
- [ ] a test asserts the override withdraws ONLY the strict-output flag: another capability read off the same
      profile is unchanged from `openai_model_profile(...)`, so the override is surgical rather than a blanket
      conservative record
- [ ] a REGRESSION GUARD test asserts a bare `openai:gpt-4o` with NO `base_url` still takes S1's lazy
      model-STRING path and constructs no provider — proving the `openai` SDK stays optional and that the
      existing parameterized `openai:gpt-4o` case in `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` is unaffected
- [ ] `providers.py` stays under the 300 LOC fixed by S1's attested criterion (or the builder lives in its own
      leaf module), and `grep -rn 'openai' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` shows no provider-name branch added there
- [ ] `pyproject.toml`'s `agents` extra is UNCHANGED (`git diff` shows the openai addition only under
      `dev`), so runtime posture stays opt-in
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite (`make test`, not just `tests/unit`) pass
- [ ] each acceptance criterion above is discharged by a NAMED test, listed in a ticket comment before close —
      S2 closed late because half of one criterion had no test despite an 18-test oracle
